Steering verification

Each request starts from the ordinary forecast. Verification measures control of a requested change in forecast units. Observed futures are used only to score forecast errors (median MAE and quantile pinball loss).

Known-answer target checks · 19/19 passed

Four-step examples test the target definitions independently of model fitting. The context alternates −1 and +1. Median forecasts increase from 0 to 3, with a planted four-step wave for the season removal check. For context policies, a transparent predictor copies its inputs. The table gives the largest absolute difference from the analytic answer across steps and channels. The pass threshold is 1e−9.

Use the fitted model on another input

Save a model/request ZIP using its export link. With this toolkit and the base checkpoint available, call the predictor on a new context of the same length.

from tsfm_lens.steering import SteeredForecaster
model = SteeredForecaster.load('profile.zip')
comparison = model.compare(my_context)
ordinary, steered = comparison.baseline, comparison.forecast

To change directions and doses, launch the local desktop studio with your run YAML. Choose a reference input or paste your own. The export dialog can include cached weights.

python -m tsfm_lens.steering.studio --config CONFIG.yaml

Held-out results

Success intervals are 95% Wilson intervals per request, assuming independent contexts. They exclude uncertainty from refitting and are unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Improved counts nonzero targets closer than the ordinary forecast. Latency excludes fitting and verification replay. Forecast loss intervals resample paired series. Smaller MAE and pinball loss are better.

How this report was constructed

Distinct float32 contexts were sampled without replacement using the run seed. Discovery measures intervention responses on calibration contexts and selects sites on validation contexts. Full-horizon context policies directly define their target by rerunning the model with the configured input change. Their agreement checks implementation. Each evaluation replays the intervention. A verified case requires a nonzero target, relative L2 error within the configured tolerance across all steps and channels (unsteered error is 100%), and replay agreement within relative tolerance 1e-5 and absolute tolerance 1e-6. Charts show the lower median and worst errors on the most targeted channel.
